flawed_step: Step 2: Applying normality to C and {x} is unjustified because, without a T1 assumption, the singleton {x} need not be closed.
counterexample: Let X={0,1} with topology {∅,{1},X}. Its closed sets are ∅,{0},X, so it is normal. But for C={0} and x=1, every open set containing C is X, which cannot be disjoint from any open set containing x. Thus X is not regular under the given definition.
assessment_summary: The standard proof fails when it needs {x} to be closed, and the Sierpiński space supplies a normal but nonregular counterexample.
